## Routing Decision — Chapter 5B, High-Recall Calibration

**Source:** LAW-005 — *Acuerdo 173/2022* (December 2022 fuel-stimulus agreement, SHCP, published Diario Oficial de la Federación)

---

### Chunk U0001 — INCLUDED

**Locator:** extracted HTML block 1

**Applicable lenses and relevance:**

| Lens | Question ID | Relevance | Adjacent Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5B.1 | Medium | Establishes fiscal stimulus percentages for automotive fuels (Dec 10–16 2022); instrument is tax-based rather than cash transfer — raises question of whether it pursues broad-based prosperity or short-term popularity/loyalty |
| 2 | 5B.2 | Low | Signed by Karina Ramírez Arras (Titular, Unidad de Política de Ingresos No Tributarios); credentialed professional indicates standard bureaucratic process, but no evidence on appointment credibility or performance-based retention |
| 3 | 5B.3 | **High** | This IS the credible fiscal/tax rule — publishes stimulus percentages, monetary amounts, and quotas for the IEPS tax on fuels; directly establishes the fiscal framework for the period |
| 4 | 5B.4 | **High** | Creates and consistently applies fuel-tax rules across all automotive fuel categories; establishes binding quotas and stimulus rates for the period |
| 5 | 5B.5 | Low | No visible anti-corruption enforcement, audit cooperation, or remediation language in this chunk; formal government decree format is neutral-to-positive on institutional compliance |
| 6 | 5B.6 | Low | No budget-output language; infrastructure/administrative capacity outcomes not addressed |
| 7 | 5B.7 | **High** | Authoritative, published economic information from SHCP; appears on behalf of the Mexican Treasury in the official gazette — credible fiscal information channel |
| 8 | 5B.8 | Medium | Differential treatment by fuel type (lower-octane gasoline gets stimulus; higher-octane gets 0%) suggests distributional targeting across socioeconomic fuel-consumer classes |
| 9 | 5B.9 | Medium | 2022 fuel-price shocks were a live macroeconomic stress event; this decree is a fiscal response, but this chunk does not show funded/targeted measures, monitoring, or correction mechanisms |
| 10 | 5B.10 | Low | No counterfactual or trajectory language in this chunk |

**Exclusion reason:** N/A — chunk is included.

**Cited lenses:** 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.7 (primary); 5B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9 (secondary); 5B.2, 5B.5, 5B.10 (low but present); 5B.6 (absent)

---

### Chunk U0002 — INCLUDED

**Locator:** extracted HTML block 2

**Applicable lenses and relevance:**

| Lens | Question ID | Relevance | Adjacent Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5B.1 | **High** | Quantitative fuel-stimulus amounts — diesel at $3.6071/liter, lower-octane gasoline at $1.4803/liter — directly determine whether the policy achieves broad-based prosperity or subsidizes specific sectors/actors for political loyalty |
| 2 | 5B.2 | Low | No appointment or personnel evidence in this chunk |
| 3 | 5B.3 | **High** | Concrete pesos-per-liter amounts operationalize the fiscal rules from U0001; establishes actual fiscal cost and tax-quota structure |
| 4 | 5B.4 | **High** | Uniform per-liter rules applied across fuel types; creates binding regulatory framework for competition in fuel markets |
| 5 | 5B.5 | Medium | Formal quotas and published rates are the kind of transparent rule that enables competition and anti-corruption monitoring, but no enforcement actions or audit cooperation are in this chunk |
| 6 | 5B.6 | Low | Budget-output evidence not present in the numeric tables |
| 7 | 5B.7 | **High** | Exact pesos-per-liter figures published for each fuel type — reliable, machine-readable economic information available for independent evaluation |
| 8 | 5B.8 | **High** | Diesel stimulus ($3.6071) vs. high-octane gasoline ($0.00) — strongly differentiated treatment suggests distributional choices across income classes (diesel used more by freight/logistics; high-octane by wealthier drivers) |
| 9 | 5B.9 | **High** | December 2022 was a period of elevated fuel prices/inflation in Mexico; the stimulus amounts (especially 59.77% diesel stimulus) are a concrete fiscal response to the fuel-price shock |
| 10 | 5B.10 | Low | No trajectory comparison or legacy language; implementation-lag and constraint accounting not present |

**Exclusion reason:** N/A — chunk is included.

**Cited lenses:** 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9 (primary); 5B.5 (secondary); 5B.2, 5B.10 (low but present); 5B.6 (absent)

---

### Summary

| chunk_id | Decision | Primary lenses | Secondary lenses | Exclusion reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U0001 | **INCLUDED** | 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.7 | 5B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9 | — |
| U0002 | **INCLUDED** | 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9 | 5B.5 | — |

**No exclusions.** Both chunks are retained. This source is a direct executive-legislative fiscal record establishing concrete fuel-tax stimuli and quotas for a specific period during a macroeconomic shock. It provides primary evidence for 5B.3 (fiscal rules), 5B.4 (regulatory framework), 5B.7 (published economic information), and 5B.9 (shock response), and secondary evidence for 5B.1 (prosperity vs. rents), 5B.8 (distributional incidence), and 5B.5 (transparency/competition conditions). Absence of evidence on 5B.6 (budget outputs) and 5B.10 (trajectory) should reduce confidence in those lens assessments rather than exclude the chunks.
